basis: Approved runtime review v1 and lead v2 guards

cases.expected: A queued task reserves its attempt and finite capacity before any resource or process effect.
Concurrent starts for the same task create one worker and one resource pair.
A full host or project cap creates no process or resources.
A real waiting worker handshake records Starting; its assigned command has not run.
Missing, stale, wrong-task or failed provider In Progress confirmation cannot grant work.
Both observed worktree and database ownership must match task, attempt and worker.
Confirmed Todo dispatches one real worker, confirms In Progress and executes a disposable fixture command.
Resource proof and Running cannot precede observed worker startup.
Every work command rechecks the current Core lease before execution.
A newer human hold stops the owned runtime before capacity release; no later command runs.
Reassignment or session revocation rejects the next boundary and quiesces the old worker.
A stale attempt or decision revision cannot resume work.
Heartbeat and checkpoint records do not establish completion.
Exit zero without required structured outcome does not issue successful host completion.
A real nonzero child exit remains a failed attempt with durable diagnostics.
A deadline stops and confirms the entire owned group, including a TERM-resistant descendant.
A leader exiting zero while a descendant lives is failed or unknown, never successful.
An unrelated process-group sentinel survives normal, timeout and error cleanup.
Unavailable process inventory or identity mismatch retains capacity and resources.
An interrupted supervisor stops the owned group or persists uncertainty without erasing the failure.
Restart after launch intent and before reply never launches a competing worker.
Restart after ambiguous resource creation reconciles existing ownership instead of recreating it.
Restart preserves the original finite deadline.
Missing or malformed startup acknowledgement retains the launch claim until reconciliation.
A disposable real Git repository produces a distinct task-owned worktree on the requested base.
A distinct SQLite application fixture has an internal ownership record and differs from the control store.
Creation intent is durably committed before Git or database effects.
A worktree created before database failure remains recorded for reconciliation.
Absolute escapes, parent traversal, symlinks and existing foreign paths are rejected.
Shared, metadata or differently owned databases are rejected.
Changed inode, ownership marker, Git common directory or branch prevents deletion.
Active, merging or unknown attempts cannot delete owned resources.
A safely settled attempt removes only verified owned disposable worktree/database resources.
Uncommitted work prevents automatic resource deletion.
Repeated verified cleanup preserves the tombstone and does not touch foreign resources.
Concurrent task resources and sentinel repositories/databases remain unchanged.
Explicit prefix and kind routing rejects overlapping issuers and unknown prefixes/kinds.
Only typed trusted observation operations issue runtime references; arbitrary Evidence issuance is unavailable.
Cross-session/task/attempt/worker references fail verification or Core guards.
Expired references and changed stored receipt content are rejected.
Worker argv, environment, worktree and outputs do not receive proof signing material.
Restart verifies prior unchanged issued receipts and retains their source observation identity.
Every Claude argv uses the resolved claude_roni profile and refuses missing/wrong profile or fallback.
Host commands use fixed structured argv; prompt and paths cannot inject shell arguments.
Claude restricted/explicit settings/MCP and Codex ignore-user-config/ephemeral use locally supported flags.
Managed profiles exclude native task writers and unmanaged agents; unsupported enforcement remains an explicit capability limit.
Valid host init/thread, tool, usage and final events are recorded distinctly.
Malformed, oversized, mismatched-session or contradictory event streams fail closed.
Provider error, missing terminal event, host nonzero and timeout cannot become a successful turn.
A provider invocation without a concrete reviewed cost authorization is refused before launch.
Estimated/token usage does not automatically settle actual incremental charges.
Runtime policy flows through Core operations; adapter storage writes only its own journal tables.
Product and bootstrap import the same group implementation; all 70 scaffold behaviors remain covered.
The bootstrap absolute entrypoint still works outside the repository.
Fresh real Claude trace in an isolated fixture proves model execution and exact final response; not run before probe/cost review.
Fresh real Codex trace in an isolated fixture proves model execution and exact final response; not run before probe/cost review.
Waiting-harness initialization and actual model startup/completion remain distinct observed records.
An expired deadline or missing accounted launch grant refuses the command before it executes.
